children: McGraw Hill, Inc. said its subsidiary plans, subject to market conditions, to offer $500M senior secured notes due 2033 and refinance its credit facilities, using proceeds and a new $830M Term Loan B to redeem 5.750% notes due 2028 and refinance its existing term loan.
Adds long-dated secured debt; pricing will signal credit risk and interest cost.
Refinances existing term loan; extends maturities, affects interest expense.
Provides liquidity backstop; replaces existing revolver.
Removes 2028 maturity wall; new rate vs 5.750% will impact costs.
Improves runway for working capital needs.

This is a balance-sheet refi extending maturities and consolidating debt, consistent with liability management seen across leveraged issuers. A clearer catalyst would be final pricing (coupon/spread), demand indications, and any change to total debt or interest expense guidance.
